evals.name: constant-count-and-source
evals.prompt: BoatStatistics already has string Id and int BookingCount. Every BoatBooked should increment the one row keyed fleet. It reads the inbox event sequence. Show the minimal model-bound C# mapping and explain whether I need a separate projection class or explicit AutoMap. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Model-bound Count<BoatBooked>(ConstantKey = fleet), EventSequence(inbox), Chronicle Key where needed. AutoMap is default; no separate class or removed FromEventSequence attribute.
assertions: Uses Count<BoatBooked> with ConstantKey as an initializer property rather than a constructor argument.
Uses the EventSequence attribute to select inbox, not the removed FromEventSequence attribute.
Uses model-bound attributes without a separate projection class and explains that AutoMap is on by default.

evals.name: joined-latch-and-filter
evals.prompt: Our existing BookingOverview projection joins BoatBlocked into IsBlocked=true while BookingUnblocked locally sets the same field false. It sticks true after unblocking. We also added [Tag("harbor")] expecting to narrow events to that appended tag. Explain both failures and propose a safe shape. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Joins resolve after local mappings and always win; CHR0042 diagnoses overlap. Separate BlockedAt/UnblockedAt facts and derive outcome at the query edge. Artifact Tag does not filter; projections have no metadata filter.
assertions: Explains that joined values are applied after local mappings whenever own events are handled, so a local false cannot clear that joined field.
Names CHR0042 or JoinOverridesLocalWrite as the overlap diagnostic.
Proposes separate blocked/unblocked facts and derives the outcome at the query edge rather than writing the same joined property twice.
Explains that Tag labels the artifact and cannot filter appended metadata in a projection; metadata filtering belongs to reducers or reactors.

evals.name: variant-late-events
evals.prompt: Our work-item projections represent BacklogItem and PullRequestItem with genuinely different fields. On Chronicle 19.1.0, how do we keep exactly one active shape, avoid a replayed title change resurrecting an old backlog entry, and prevent a startup declaration error? Show the relevant attributes or fluent declarations. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Each variant anchors to VariantOf<WorkItem> and has EntersOn. Entering removes other shapes; non-entering events become update-only joins and cannot resurrect. Missing EntersOn throws VariantMustDeclareEntersOnEvent.
assertions: Declares VariantOf with the same identity type and EntersOn for each variant.
Explains that entering one variant removes the entity from other variants in the group.
Explains that non-entering mappings become update-only joins and cannot create or resurrect the old variant.
Names VariantMustDeclareEntersOnEvent as the startup error when a variant has no entering event.

evals.name: child-every-and-definition-evolution
evals.prompt: At Chronicle 19.50.0 our parent has FromEvery timestamps and a child-only event. Does that event update the parent? Can attributes opt out? Also a query-assembled member triggers CHR0024, and we changed a counter under Manual definitionEvolution. Explain the supported shapes and historical repair. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Child-only events feed owning parent every mappings; fluent ExcludeChildProjections opts out, attributes do not. NotProjected exempts query members from AutoMap/CHR0024. Manual creates replay recommendation; deployment alone does not repair history.
assertions: States child-only and nested-child events feed owning parent FromEvery mappings at 19.50.0.
Names ExcludeChildProjections as the fluent opt-out and states model-bound FromEvery always includes children.
Uses NotProjected on the query-assembled property or parameter and explains AutoMap skips it and CHR0024 is suppressed by that declaration.
Explains Manual definitionEvolution leaves a replay recommendation and corrected counters/joins require replay to repair historical values.

evals.name: ordered-catchup-and-failed-lookup
evals.prompt: On Chronicle 19.50.1 we increased maxConcurrentPartitions to accelerate a projection catch-up. A new source failed during catch-up and the next-event storage lookup also errored. Can healthy sources keep catching up, can the observer fast-forward, and will completing replay end quarantine? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Projection replay/catch-up each use one globally ordered step; new catch-up failure stops that step. Storage error does not prove absence or advance position. Quarantine does not end on completion.
assertions: Explains projection catch-up and replay each use a single globally ordered job step, not concurrent per-source steps.
Explains a new failure during projection catch-up stops the ordered step, distinct from ordinary live partition isolation.
States a next-event lookup error leaves the saved position unchanged and retries rather than fast-forwarding; only NotFound proves absence.
States replay/catch-up completion does not end observer quarantine or repair historical skipped events automatically.
